tests.rationale: Guards the local-only provider policy and cloud-provider hiding boundary.
Guards effective context-window and overflow policy behavior for local models.
Guards timeout scaling for slow local models and body-timeout recovery behavior.
Guards swarm pause/resume and autonomous guardrail behavior.
Guards workspace identity, project health diagnostics, and ownership-sensitive project state.
Guards decomposition graph application, plan artifacts, and Planning-lane behavior.
Guards the strict-isolation invariant that agent tools and the acceptance gate never execute on the host filesystem/shell (no host fallback).
Guards Docker sandbox lockdown flags, fail-closed availability checks, per-task uid isolation, and pool/queue admission.
Guards the fail-closed task-start preflight (sandbox-unavailable refusal) and candidate-window fit budget.

Held-out compositional oracle for project 18: wafer conservation across chained split/merge/rework, the surface the spec's own per-module acceptance tests cannot reach.
Held-out compositional oracle for project 04: deep-chain, diamond, rework-edge and deep-gap tracing — the recall-safety surface the spec's own shallow trace tests cannot reach.
Held-out compositional oracle for project 27: RNG stream INDEPENDENCE and replay across interleaved draws — the surface a shared-counter implementation passes every per-stream test on.
Held-out oracle for project 32: the fixed-point determinism substrate under composition — integer domain, exact replay, specified truncation, and the conservation guard's THROW.
Held-out oracle for project 21: cross-artifact correspondence — hunk/symbol overlap at boundaries and across files, and blast-radius traversal over cycles, diamonds and multiple seeds.
Held-out oracle for project 30: A* path OPTIMALITY (a wrong search still returns a working route) plus station capacity under a long interleaving of occupies and releases.

Held-out oracle for project 24: redaction TOTALITY and statelessness — the spec's own suggested containsHostPath uses shared /g regexes, whose lastIndex makes the guard answer differently on repeated calls.

Held-out oracle for project 19: exactly-once client dedup keyed on the COMPOSITE (clientId, requestSeq) — every visible acceptance check uses one client, so a seq-only store passes them all and leaks one client's result to another.

Held-out oracle for project 07: bitemporal balanceAsOf (effectiveAt AND postedAt AND discardedAt>knownAt) plus append-only immutability — a reversal must ADD a compensating entry, never remove history.
Held-out oracle for project 22: workspace-digest integrity — key-order independence and path/content framing, the two collisions that let a stale context pack look fresh.

Held-out oracle for project 23: the authority fence under STRUCTURED output — both visible tests pass flat lowercase strings, which String(output).includes() satisfies while letting every real (object-shaped) injection through.

Held-out oracle for project 25: safety PRECEDENCE in the self-modification gate — each visible test exercises one rule alone, so a gate with inverted ordering passes all three and lets an approved, improving change edit the integrity firewall.

Held-out oracle for project 31: flat-array spatial indexing on a NON-SQUARE world plus the double-buffer generation discipline — a transposed index is correct on a square grid and a round-trip cannot detect it.

Held-out oracle for project 26: the rules the six canonical perft positions do NOT reach — horizontal en-passant pin, castling through an attacked square, under-promotion completeness. NOTE: null-agent gate verified; discrimination against a reference engine NOT yet demonstrated.
Held-out oracle for project 20: hardware-contract fidelity — x0 hardwiring inspected in the STORED state, fault reason correctness (misaligned vs out_of_bounds), and the exact memory boundary.

Held-out oracle for project 13: boolean operator PRECEDENCE in rule conditions — a left-to-right evaluator agrees with the correct one on every single-operator fixture and silently mis-fires every mixed rule.
Held-out oracle for project 09: COLREGS RECIPROCITY — every visible case classifies from one vessel's view, so a frame error can make BOTH vessels believe they stand on and neither gives way.
Held-out oracle for project 15: CPM joins take the MAX of predecessors (fixture lists the longest SECOND) and the forward pass must be topological rather than positional.

Held-out oracle for project 05: the FSM COMPLEMENT (all 58 illegal pairs, where the visible suite checks every legal edge but only two illegal ones) plus agreement between transition, legalNextStatuses and the refusal payload.

Held-out oracle for project 06: quality-lattice monotonicity — permutation invariance, the one-way no-improvement property, and the STRICT bad-fraction threshold (which the returned code alone cannot discriminate).

Held-out oracle for project 12: mergeBase must be the MOST RECENT common ancestor. NOTE: the spec's own suggested BFS-first-hit algorithm fails this probe — graded against the stated contract, and the spec defect is recorded in todo.md.
Held-out oracle for project 29: a belt is FIFO, not a bag — countItemsOnLine conserves perfectly for a stack-backed line — plus backpressure that must refuse without consuming.
Held-out oracle for project 28: diffusion ISOTROPY — an in-place row-major sweep conserves mass perfectly and drifts pheromone down and right, which no conservation check can see.

Held-out oracle for project 34: fog-of-war leakage asserted over the SERIALISED observation (the visible suite checks one field of six), plus ghosts that must hold the last-SEEN position rather than live ground truth.

Held-out oracle for project 33: the SHAPE of the urgency curve. The spec's visible acceptance pins only urgency(0) and urgency(100) — the two points where a linear ramp and the specified quadratic agree exactly.
